facts.statement: Iaceornis is a genus of dinosaur.
The only known species is Iaceornis marshi.
The genus was named by Clarke in 2004.
The fossil specimen was first discovered by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1877.
facts.quote: Since it was first discovered by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1877

facts.statement: In 2004, Julia A. Clarke distinguished the skeleton from Apatornis based on differences in wing bone characteristics.
facts.quote: In 2004, paleontologist Julia A. Clarke showed that the skeleton actually differed in important characteristics of the wing bones from the true, holotype specimen of Apatornis.

facts.statement: Clarke named the new species Iaceornis marshi, which translates to "Marsh's neglected bird".
facts.quote: Therefore, she assigned the more complete remains to a new genus and species, Iaceornis marshi, meaning "Marsh's neglected bird".

facts.statement: Iaceornis lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 83.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was endemic to North America during the Late Cretaceous, living about 83.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: The time range for Iaceornis is the Santonian stage, between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: The animal is known from a single partial skeleton found in Gove County, Kansas, that lacks a skull.
facts.quote: It is known from a single fossil specimen found in Gove County, Kansas, and consisting of a partial skeleton lacking a skull.

facts.statement: Iaceornis was a marine ornithuran dinosaur closely related to modern birds.
facts.quote: Iaceornis is a genus of marine ornithuran dinosaurs closely related to modern birds.

rejected.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Iaceornis as more advanced than Ichthyornis but less advanced than modern birds.
rejected.quote: In Clarke's phylogenetic analysis, she found that Iaceornis is more advanced than Ichthyornis but less advanced than modern birds.
